Monthly cloud spend -60% (US$1,200 → US$400): moderation routed by media type, generated results stored and cached.
AI customer service live: a Python RAG stack retrieves the FAQ and knowledge base for common questions, handing off to a human when confidence falls short.
Delivered end to end on my own: Flutter app, NestJS backend, Docker deployment, including content moderation and real-person face verification.
POC mini-game taken to production and grown into a 12-title product line: led 11 engineers through delivery.
Held up a thousand bets/orders per second during draws and peak hours: Kafka for event streams, Redis and Bull Queue for caching and asynchronous settlement.
Release mistakes -70%: set up a release checklist and a standard release process.

Introduced design review and code review: both became the development standard reused across product lines.
Built and operated: games, lotteries, blockchain fair random numbers, crawler data, and admin dashboards.
System analysis, backend implementation, and performance work: refactored inherited legacy code into modules that are easier to maintain.

Commercial projects delivered from 0 to 1: lending systems, a video streaming platform, an equipment repair system, and e-commerce modules, spanning requirements analysis, system design, and production operations.
Stack varied by project: C#, Node.js, React, and Salesforce (Apex, VisualForce), each on a separate client engagement.
Reduced module coupling: separated frontend and backend responsibilities, redesigned the API, and established unit and functional testing.
Applied Clean Code and design patterns: unified naming, layering, and responsibility boundaries into a maintainable code style.
